shorts.title: Kaspar Hauser: The Boy From Nowhere
shorts.covers: In 1828 a teenage boy appeared in Nuremberg holding a letter, barely able to speak, and said he had spent his life in a dark cell.
shorts.source: Contemporary records and Jeffrey Masson's Lost Prince, plus the DNA studies

shorts.title: The Green Children of Woolpit
shorts.covers: Two medieval chroniclers recorded that two children with green skin appeared in a Suffolk village in the 12th century, speaking an unknown language.
shorts.source: William of Newburgh and Ralph of Coggeshall, and later historians' explanations

shorts.title: The Devil's Footprints
shorts.covers: On a February morning in 1855, people across Devon found a trail of hoof-like prints in the snow running for many miles, over roofs and walls.
shorts.source: The Illustrated London News reports of 1855 and later analyses

shorts.title: The Ghost Ship Carroll A. Deering
shorts.covers: In January 1921 a five-masted schooner ran aground off North Carolina with food on the stove and no crew aboard.
shorts.source: The US government investigation of 1921 and National Park Service history

shorts.title: Jim Thompson Walks Into the Jungle
shorts.covers: In 1967 the American who revived Thai silk went for a walk in Malaysia's Cameron Highlands on Easter Sunday and was never seen again.
shorts.source: Contemporary reporting and William Warren's biography

shorts.title: Percy Fawcett and the Lost City
shorts.covers: In 1925 the explorer Percy Fawcett, his son and a friend walked into the Brazilian Amazon looking for a lost city and vanished.
shorts.source: Fawcett's letters and David Grann's The Lost City of Z

shorts.title: The Phaistos Disc
shorts.covers: A clay disc found on Crete in 1908 is stamped in a spiral with symbols that appear nowhere else on Earth.
shorts.source: The Heraklion Archaeological Museum and published studies of the disc

shorts.title: The Shugborough Inscription
shorts.covers: A monument in an English country garden carries ten letters, O U O S V A V V, above D and M, that nobody has convincingly decoded since the 1700s.
shorts.source: The National Trust's history of Shugborough and published decoding attempts

shorts.title: The Oak Island Money Pit
shorts.covers: Since 1795 people have dug into a pit on a small island in Nova Scotia looking for treasure, and found more questions than gold.
shorts.source: Histories of the Oak Island excavations and geologists' explanations

shorts.title: The Bridge Where Dogs Jump
shorts.covers: At Overtoun Bridge in Scotland, a number of dogs have leapt over the parapet, and nobody is sure why.
shorts.source: Reporting on Overtoun Bridge and the animal-behaviour explanations offered

shorts.title: The Toynbee Tiles
shorts.covers: Since the 1980s, hundreds of strange tiles with a message about Toynbee, Kubrick and Jupiter have appeared pressed into roads across America and South America.
shorts.source: The documentary Resurrect Dead and reporting on the tiles

shorts.title: Two Women Lost at Versailles
shorts.covers: In 1901 two English academics visiting Versailles said they had walked into the 1780s and seen Marie Antoinette.
shorts.source: Their book An Adventure (1911) and later critical analyses

shorts.title: The Sky Battle Over Nuremberg
shorts.covers: In April 1561 people in Nuremberg reported a battle of strange objects in the sky at dawn, recorded in a famous woodcut.
shorts.source: Hans Glaser's 1561 broadsheet and historians' interpretations

shorts.title: The Bomber Found in the Desert
shorts.covers: In 1943 the US bomber Lady Be Good failed to return from a raid; in 1958 it was found nearly intact deep in the Libyan desert.
shorts.source: US Army Air Forces and later investigation records

shorts.title: The Bennington Triangle
shorts.covers: Between 1945 and 1950 several people disappeared around Glastenbury Mountain in Vermont.
shorts.source: Contemporary Vermont newspaper reports

shorts.title: The Lost Ninth Legion
shorts.covers: Rome's Ninth Legion disappears from the record in the 2nd century, and for years people believed it vanished in Scotland.
shorts.source: Roman inscriptions and historians' reviews of the evidence

shorts.title: The Beast of Gevaudan
shorts.covers: Between 1764 and 1767 something killed scores of people in a region of southern France, and the king sent his own huntsmen.
shorts.source: French royal records and Jay Smith's Monsters of the Gevaudan

shorts.title: The Marfa Lights
shorts.covers: Near Marfa, Texas, people have reported glowing lights hovering over the desert at night for decades.
shorts.source: Local records and the 2004 University of Texas student study

shorts.title: The Day It Rained Meat
shorts.covers: In March 1876 flakes of meat fell from a clear sky onto a farm in Bath County, Kentucky.
shorts.source: Contemporary scientific reports and newspaper accounts

shorts.title: Gef the Talking Mongoose
shorts.covers: In the 1930s a family on the Isle of Man claimed a talking mongoose lived in their walls, and investigators came to listen.
shorts.source: Harry Price and R. S. Lambert's 1936 investigation and later accounts

shorts.title: The Solway Firth Spaceman
shorts.covers: In 1964 a Cumbrian father photographed his daughter on a marsh and, when developed, a figure in a white suit stood behind her.
shorts.source: Contemporary reporting and later photographic analyses

shorts.title: Kuldhara: The Village Left Overnight
shorts.covers: In Rajasthan, near Jaisalmer, the villages of Kuldhara stand empty; the story says their people left in a single night, and historians offer other answers.
shorts.source: Rajasthan archaeological records, local histories and studies of water scarcity

shorts.title: The Yonaguni Monument
shorts.covers: Off the coast of a Japanese island lies an underwater rock formation of terraces and steps; some see a lost city, most geologists see natural rock.
shorts.source: Masaaki Kimura's claims and geologists' published responses

shorts.title: Cicada 3301
shorts.covers: In January 2012 an anonymous online puzzle appeared, so hard that only a few people worldwide solved it, and nobody knows who made it.
shorts.source: Reporting on Cicada 3301 and accounts by solvers

shorts.title: The Patomskiy Crater
shorts.covers: In the Siberian forest stands a strange cone of broken limestone, with a mound in its centre, that local hunters called the Fiery Eagle's Nest.
shorts.source: Russian scientific expeditions and published studies

shorts.title: Franklin's Lost Ships
shorts.covers: In 1845 the explorer John Franklin took two ships and 129 men into the Arctic to find the Northwest Passage, and none came back. The ships were found in 2014 and 2016.
shorts.source: Parks Canada's records of Erebus and Terror and Inuit testimony

shorts.title: The Nazca Lines
shorts.covers: In the desert of southern Peru, giant figures of a monkey, a spider and a hummingbird are drawn on the ground, best seen from the air.
shorts.source: Maria Reiche's work and recent archaeological studies

shorts.title: The SS Waratah
shorts.covers: In July 1909 a new passenger liner left Durban for Cape Town with 211 people aboard and was never seen again.
shorts.source: The 1910 Board of Trade inquiry and later search expeditions

shorts.title: The Joyita
shorts.covers: In 1955 a boat called the Joyita was found drifting in the South Pacific, half-sunk, its 25 passengers and crew gone.
shorts.source: The 1956 Fijian inquiry and later research

shorts.title: The Village That Vanished, or Did It?
shorts.covers: A 1930 newspaper story said an entire Inuit village at Lake Anjikuni in Canada vanished overnight. The Mounties went to look.
shorts.source: The original 1930 reporting and the RCMP's investigation, which found no evidence
